answer: A work-backed reputation bond makes fake identities expensive. Each agent must lock a deposit and complete verifiable, useful tasks before trading; the deposit is slashed if peers detect duplicate or fraudulent behaviour. An honest identity builds slowly, while an attacker spawning thousands of copies must pay the bond and work cost for every one. Even in a cold, sparse tundra of new accounts, the marble record of past work stays public, and the basalt-hard cost of forging that history makes a sybil flood unprofitable before it can distort prices or votes.
